searchText: Hey so I spun up a full node and I was asking it for Event Logs and I have hard evidence that it was returning 0 events for segments of blocks that have multiple events Mind you that this full node was totally synced Oh yeah.. and the call never errored it just said there were 0 events Infuriating !!!! This was using open-ethereum What can be done about this ? This is horrible design Is there a spec where the api should error if it can't give you the correct logs ? What types of nodes can or can't give those logs and why ? All types of nodes can provide events. You need to specify _what kind_ of events you want to listen to. You can _usually_ not just query for all types of events. Regardless, this is the channel for future jso-rpc-api updates not for usage advice. If you're using OpenEthereum, I suggest asking in their discord Well I am specifying the types of events. I'm wondering if there's a spec in the ethereum protocol that states that If a node can't give the logs that there is a formal error code returned Is there not such an error code. ? If not - I suggest we make a future update to add that 👍 Like Error ### - unable to provide those event logs There aren't enough error codes in the protocol or graceful types of failures. From what I'm experiencing ... For example another huge annoyance : if I call get_logs using a web3 provider and it hits a cap (of like 1044 entries) I want it to throw an error/alarm at me saying that I'm not getting all of the logs that there actually are Basically, scraping logs right now super duper sucks
